examples.problem:
All of the edges of a cube are increasing at a rate of $2\,\text{mm}/\text{s}.$ How fast is the surface area of the cube changing when the volume of the cube is $8\,\text{cm}^3?$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/differential/14096050/assets/a6ef2af1ed8e44f82469625e232ed67c0b809a3c8199a6ce52fd2bf2e3fcffa7.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Let $x$ be the side length of the cube, let $S$ be its surface area, and let $V$ be its volume. All of the variables change with time. In particular, we are given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}=2\,\text{mm}/\text{s}.\end{aligned}
$$

We would like to find $\dfrac{\textrm d S}{\textrm dt}$ when $V= 8\,\text{cm}^3.$

We want to find the rate of change of $S$ knowing the rate of change of $x.$ So, we start with the formula for the surface area of the cube:

$$
S= 6x^2
$$

Now, we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}S & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(6{x}^{2}) \\ \frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =12x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}.\end{aligned}
$$

Before we plug in the known values, we need to find the value of $x$ when $V= 8\,\text{cm}^3.$ We get

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={x}^{3} \\ 8 & ={x}^{3} \\ x & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

So $x=2\,\text{cm}=20\,\text{mm}.$

We can now plug the known values into the above expression. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =12x\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} \\ \frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =12(20)(2) \\ \frac{\text{d}S}{\text{d}t} & =480.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the cube's surface area is changing at a rate of  $480 \,\text{mm}^2/\text{s}.$

A rectangular fish tank is draining. The tank is $6\,\text{ft}$ long and $4\,\text{ft}$ wide. What is the rate of change of the water level if the volume is decreasing at a rate of $1.2\,{\text{ft}}^{3}/\text{min}?$ Assume that the water level's rate of decrease is positive.

The water level is decreasing at a rate of
{{field-1}}
$\text{ft}/\text{min}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let $x,y,z$ be the dimensions of the rectangular prism, let $V$ be its volume. We are given that 

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =6\,\text{ft}, \\ y & =4\,\text{ft}.\end{aligned}
$$

Also, we know that

$$
\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t}=-1.2\,{\text{ft}}^{3}/\text{min}.
$$

We would like to find $\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}$ when $x=6\,\text{ft}$ and $y=4\,\text{ft}.$

We start with the formula for the volume of the rectangular prism:

$$
V=xyz
$$

Substituting the known values, we get

$$
V=(6)(4)z=24z.
$$

Now, we differentiate with respect to time using the chain rule, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(24z) \\ \frac{\text{d}V}{\text{d}t} & =24(\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}).\end{aligned}
$$

We can now plug in the known value into the above expression. This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-1.2 & =24(\frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t}) \\ \frac{\text{d}z}{\text{d}t} & =-0.05\,\text{ft}\text{/h}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the water level is decreasing at a rate of $0.05\,\text{ft}/\text{min}.$
